clue.text: Staff covered in leaves given to leading lady that could be fiery

indicators.note: the staff word is wrapped up inside the leaves word, as if covered by them

parts.note: salad is a dish of leaves
to staff a post is to man it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the nation's leading lady

explanation.surface: A cook adds a wooden stick to a salad and serves it to the star actress, warning it might be spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered in' puts MAN inside SALAD; ER (Elizabeth Regina) is a standard crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend this lizard-like amphibian lives in flames, so it is a creature that could be fiery.

clue.text: Spectacle for the audience in place

indicators.note: an audience hears the word, so it is the spoken form that counts

parts.note: a sight is a spectacle, something worth seeing

explanation.surface: A theatre show staged as a spectacle for the audience in a particular venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location, the spot where something stands or happens.

clue.text: Slower accepting university chair

indicators.note: the slower word takes the university letter into itself

parts.note: something slower takes longer

explanation.surface: A slow candidate is finally accepted for a university professorship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chair' looks like an academic post, fitting 'university', but it is furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounger is a reclining seat for relaxing, such as a sun lounger by a pool.

clue.text: Bungling agent means I'm upset, accepting end of dream

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take in the extra letter
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
end of picks the final letter of the word dream

explanation.surface: A clumsy secret agent tells someone their methods have upset him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges AGENT MEANS I'M; 'accepting' takes in M, the last letter of 'dream'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bungling, as a noun, is clumsy handling of affairs: poor management.

clue.text: Try to impress doctor following call with work

indicators.note: the doctor letters come after the call word

parts.note: to call something is to name it
OP, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A doctor makes a house call and then tries to show off his skills.
explanation.definitionFit: Name-dropping is mentioning famous acquaintances to seem important and impress listeners.

clue.text: Age sending up 'Carry On Hospital'

indicators.note: in a down clue sending up turns the letters upward, read backwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
to cope is to carry on despite difficulty

explanation.surface: A film era mocking the British comedy 'Carry On' series' hospital films.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films are a long-running British comedy series, one being set in a hospital; here the title is just a synonym for COPE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long period of history, an era or age.

clue.text: Revolutionary final destination for posh car

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the crem, short for crematorium, is where the dead are finally taken

explanation.surface: A grand car turns out to be headed to a funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: CREM is British slang for a crematorium.
explanation.definitionFit: A Merc is the informal name for a Mercedes, a luxury German car.

clue.text: People from terrible regimes?

indicators.note: something terrible is in a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Refugees who have fled oppressive governments.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines; the last two words also give the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Émigrés are people who have left their country, often to escape political oppression.

clue.text: Conservative banks on cry for success

parts.note: an aircraft banks when it leans to one side
to weep is to cry

explanation.surface: A Tory relies on a rallying cry to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' looks financial but is the tilting of a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean sweep is total victory, winning every prize or seat.

clue.text: Support cheese-loving politician?

definitions.meaning: a surgical or structural brace that holds something up
Liz, the short-lived UK Prime Minister, famously declared cheese imports a disgrace

explanation.surface: Backing a politician known for liking cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Liz Truss, briefly UK Prime Minister in 2022, made a widely mocked speech about British cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A truss is a supporting framework or a belt worn to hold a hernia in place.

clue.text: Farah running with a black eye doesn't finish? Nonsense!

parts.note: Mo Farah, the British distance runner
a machine that is running is on

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter, never completing

parts.note: a shiner is a black eye

explanation.surface: Mo Farah, running with a black eye and failing to finish: what rubbish!
explanation.walkthrough: Mo Farah is a British Olympic distance-running champion, which makes 'running' look like part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine is foolish talk or fanciful ideas, as well as illicit liquor.

clue.text: Cliff listened out without help

indicators.note: out means wrong or off, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cliff heard something without anyone's help.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-inflicted injury is caused by oneself, done alone with nobody else involved.

clue.text: Drench girl dancing around with relatives

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the word for with
dancing letters move about and rearrange

parts.note: and means with, together

explanation.surface: Soaking a girl who is dancing among family members.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandchildren are the offspring of one's children, so family members.

clue.text: Irate Biden possibly the worse for wear

indicators.note: possibly says these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An angry President Biden looks rather unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Inebriated means drunk, and 'the worse for wear' is an idiom for drunk.

clue.text: One with a telling part in play?

definitions.text: One with a telling part in play?

parts.words: One with a telling part in play?
parts.note: a telling part sounds like a key role, but it is literally a part that tells the story on stage

explanation.surface: An actor whose role in a drama proves decisive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'telling' seems to mean significant; read it literally as storytelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrator is the voice that relates events in a play, film or novel.

clue.text: Tool that's pieced together

definitions.meaning: a saw with a fine blade for cutting curves
a puzzle assembled from interlocking pieces

explanation.surface: A tool that has been assembled from parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both a cutting saw for curves and the puzzle whose pieces it once cut.

clue.text: Journalist getting on with hotel worker

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a porter carries guests' bags in a hotel

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer gets along well with a hotel employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting on with' reads as friendship; 'on' alone gives RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter is a journalist who gathers and writes news.

clue.text: Bribe Europeans for something bouncy

parts.note: a bung is British slang for a bribe
E is the abbreviation for European, so two of them make EE

explanation.surface: Paying off Europeans to obtain a toy that bounces.
explanation.definitionFit: The elastic cord used in bungee jumping makes the jumper spring up and down.

clue.text: Young crabs?

definitions.meaning: crabs pinch with their claws, so they are pinchers; the question mark marks the playful sense

explanation.definitionFit: Small children are informally called nippers, and a crab's pincers are its nippers too.

clue.text: Complaint about undressed naked hunk

parts.note: a beef is a grievance or complaint
C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: undressed strips the outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a muscular man posing without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undressed naked' looks like doubling up but strips N and D off NAKED, leaving AKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefcake is slang for an attractive muscular man, a hunk.

clue.text: Step inside hospital department to find actor

indicators.note: the step word goes inside the hospital letters

parts.note: A and E, accident and emergency, is the UK casualty ward
a stair is a single step

explanation.surface: Walking into a casualty ward to locate a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire was a Hollywood actor and dancer, so an example of an actor.

clue.text: Somebody taking off Monet, perhaps

definitions.meaning: someone who mimics others; to take off is to imitate
Claude Monet was a painter of the French movement named after his work Impression, Sunrise

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a mimic who imitates celebrities and a member of Monet's school of painting.

clue.text: Back authoritarian

definitions.meaning: the rear part of a ship

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the rear of a vessel and harsh or strict in manner.

clue.text: Point we put before holy person

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: We stand ahead of a holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: West is one of the four cardinal compass points.

clue.text: Natter anxiously about yours truly ahead of time in therapy

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about, around, the word for yours truly
anxiously suggests agitation, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way to say me, the speaker

explanation.surface: Chatting nervously about oneself before a therapy session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natter' looks like idle chat before a session, but it is only raw letters; 'anxiously' scrambles them to TREATN, which 'about' wraps around the self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is medical care given to a patient, which therapy also means.

clue.text: Most of winter, terrible wind

indicators.note: terrible means in a bad state, so the letters are mixed
most of drops the last letter of the word

parts.note: the coldest season, taken as written

explanation.surface: Most of the winter brings a dreadful gale.
explanation.definitionFit: To twine is to wind or twist around something, as a vine does.

clue.text: Food some rejected is horrible

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diner sends back a horrible meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' hints at a reversal, but the letters read forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is a prepared item of food served at a meal.

clue.text: Engine dirt damaged component

indicators.note: damaged means knocked out of shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Dirt in an engine has damaged one of its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingredient is one element of a mixture, a constituent part.
